title: Dijkstra
objective: Find shortest distances when roads have different lengths, by settling the closest place each time.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): Dijkstra's algorithm (single-source shortest paths)

simplifies: This picks the closest place by scanning all of them (O(n²)). Real versions use a heap to find it faster. All road lengths are positive; Dijkstra can give wrong answers with negative ones.

quiz.prompt: Why is the closest unsettled place final as soon as it is settled?

options.text: Every other route goes through a place that is already at least as far, and roads only add length
options.explanation: Right. With positive road lengths, nothing can sneak in shorter later.

options.text: Because it has the fewest roads
options.explanation: Fewest roads isn't shortest distance when roads have lengths.

options.text: It isn't: distances can still change
options.explanation: For settled places they can't, as long as no road has negative length.

quiz.prompt: Roads: A–B is 1, B–C is 1, A–C is 5. Shortest distance from A to C?

options.explanation: Right. A → B → C is 1 + 1, shorter than the direct road of 5.
That is the direct road, but going through B is shorter.
There is no road of length 1 from A to C.
